# Jubilees Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Prologue — Revelation to Moses on Sinai

---

**1:1** It came to pass in the first year of the exodus of the children of Israel from Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of the month, that God spoke to Moses, saying: "Come up to me on the mountain, and I will give you two stone tablets of the law and the commandment which I have written, that you may teach them."

**1:2** And Moses went up to the mountain of God. The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and a cloud overshadowed it for six days.

**1:3** On the seventh day he called to Moses from within the cloud, and the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a burning fire on the summit of the mountain.

**1:4** Moses remained on the mountain for forty days and forty nights, and God instructed him in the earlier history and the later history of all the divisions of the days of the law and the testimony.

**1:5** He said: "Pay attention to all the words I speak to you today, and write them in a book, so that their generations may see that I have not abandoned them despite all the evil they committed in transgressing the covenant I am establishing between me and you this day on Mount Sinai."

**1:6** "When all these things come upon them, they will acknowledge that I am more righteous than they in all my judgments and all my dealings, and they will know that I have truly been with them."

**1:7** "Now write for yourself all these words that I am declaring to you today, for I know their rebellion and their stubbornness before I bring them into the land I promised to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying: 'To your descendants I will give a land flowing with milk and honey.'"

**1:8** "They will eat and be satisfied, then turn to foreign gods — gods who cannot deliver them from any of their troubles — and this record will stand as a witness against them."

**1:9** "For they will forget all my commandments — everything I command them — and follow the nations, their impurity, and their shameful practices. They will serve their gods, and those gods will become for them a snare, an affliction, a torment, and a trap."

**1:10** "Many will perish; they will be seized and fall into enemy hands, because they abandoned my statutes and commandments, the festivals of my covenant, my sabbaths, my holy things that I sanctified among them, my tabernacle, and my sanctuary that I made holy in their midst — and my name that rests upon them."

**1:11** "They will construct for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and idols, and they will bow down to the work of their own hands — each to his own image — and these things will become a stumbling block to them."

**1:12** "I will send witnesses among them to testify against them, but they will not listen; they will kill those witnesses too, and they will persecute those who seek the law, abolishing and perverting everything in order to do evil in my sight."

**1:13** "I will hide my face from them and deliver them into the hands of the nations — to captivity, to plunder, and to destruction. I will drive them from the midst of the land and scatter them among all the nations."

**1:14** "They will forget all my law, all my commandments, and all my ordinances, and they will go astray regarding the new moons, sabbaths, festivals, jubilees, and appointed times."

**1:15** "But after this they will return to me from among the nations with all their heart, all their soul, and all their strength. I will gather them from among all the nations, and they will seek me — and I will be found by them when they seek me with their whole heart and soul."

**1:16** "I will reveal to them an abundance of peace, and I will build them up as a planting of righteousness with all my heart and all my soul. They shall be a blessing and not a curse; they shall be the head and not the tail."

**1:17** "I will build my sanctuary in their midst. I will dwell with them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my true and righteous people."

**1:18** "I will not abandon them, nor will I be estranged from them, for I am the LORD their God."

**1:19** Then Moses fell on his face and prayed: "O LORD my God, do not abandon your people and your inheritance so that they wander in the error of their hearts. Do not hand them over to their enemies the nations, lest those nations rule over them and lead them into sin against you."

**1:20** "Let your mercy be lifted up over your people, O LORD. Create in them an upright spirit, and do not let the spirit of Beliar rule over them to accuse them before you and lead them astray from every righteous path, causing them to perish from before your face."

**1:21** "They are your people and your inheritance — those whom you delivered with your great power from the hand of the Egyptians. Create for them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and do not let them be trapped in their sins from this time forward and forever."

**1:22** Then the LORD said to Moses: "I know their perversity and their thoughts and their obstinacy. They will not be obedient until they confess their own sin and the sins of their ancestors."

**1:23** "But after this they will return to me in complete sincerity, with all their heart and all their soul. I will circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their descendants, and I will create a holy spirit within them. I will purify them so that they will never again turn away from me — from that day forward and forever."

**1:24** "Their souls will cling to me and to all my commandments, and they will carry out my commandments. I will be their Father and they shall be my children."

**1:25** "All of them will be called children of the living God, and every angel and every spirit will know — they shall all know — that these are my children, and that I am their Father in sincerity and righteousness, and that I love them."

**1:26** "Now write for Moses all the words I am telling you: the things of the beginning and the things of the end, everything that will come to pass in all the divisions of the days of the law and the testimony — throughout the weeks and the jubilees — until I descend and dwell with them for all eternity."

**1:27** He said to the angel of the presence: "Write for Moses from the beginning of creation until the time when my sanctuary is built among them forever."

**1:28** "The LORD will appear in the sight of all, and everyone will know that I am the God of Israel, the Father of all the children of Jacob, and King on Mount Zion forever. And Zion and Jerusalem will be holy."

**1:29** The angel of the presence, who marched before the camp of Israel, took the tablets recording the divisions of the years — from the time of creation, through the law and the testimony, through the weeks of jubilees, year by year, according to all the numbered jubilees — and he narrated to Moses the divisions of all the days of the law and the testimony until he had finished.

---
*LOGOS notes: "Angel of the presence" is the Jubilees' angelic mediator of revelation, distinct from the angel of the LORD. "Beliar" (v.20) = principal adversarial spirit. "Plant of righteousness" (v.16) = technical Enochic idiom for restored Israel.*
